blocks.content: Light is a form of energy that enables us to see objects. It is a type of electromagnetic radiation that travels in straight lines. Light plays an important role in vision, optical instruments and many natural phenomena.
1. Nature of Light

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Light exhibits dual nature: both wave-like (interference, diffraction) and particle-like (photoelectric effect) properties.
Reflection follows two laws: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane.
Refraction occurs due to the change in speed of light when traveling from one transparent medium to another, governed by Snell's Law.
Convex lenses act as converging lenses forming real or virtual images, while Concave lenses act as diverging lenses forming virtual, erect images.
Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent seven colors (VIBGYOR) when passing through a glass prism.

blocks.content: • Light is a form of energy.
• It travels in straight lines.
• Light does not require a material medium for propagation.
• The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 3 × 10^8 m/s.
2. Sources of Light
3. Reflection of Light
Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it strikes a surface.
Laws of Reflection:
• Angle of incidence = Angle of reflection.
Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation that enables vision and travels at a speed of 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum.
• Incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
4. Types of Reflection
5. Refraction of Light
Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another.
Examples:

rows: Thicker at the center, thinner at the edges
Thinner at the center, thicker at the edges
Converges parallel light rays to a real focal point
Diverges parallel light rays away from a virtual focus
Real & inverted (mostly), Virtual & erect when object < f

• Mirage in deserts.
6. Lenses
7. Optical Instruments
• Microscope – used to see small objects.
• Telescope – used to observe distant objects.
• Camera – used to capture images.
8. Dispersion of Light

items: Total Internal Reflection (TIR) requires light to travel from a denser to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle; it is the principle behind Optical Fibers and Mirages.
Myopia (Short-sightedness) is corrected using a Concave lens, whereas Hypermetropia (Far-sightedness) is corrected using a Convex lens.
Red light scatters the least due to its longer wavelength, making it ideal for danger signals, while Blue light scatters the most in the atmosphere.
Power of a lens is measured in Diopters (D) and is calculated as the reciprocal of focal length in meters (P = 1/f).

blocks.content: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component colors when it passes through a prism. The seven colors are Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red.
Important Facts
• Speed of light is approximately 3 × 10^8 m/s.
• Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
• Convex lens converges light rays.
• Dispersion of light produces seven colors.
